heading: Workplace Therapy
body:
Mental health at work often gets overlooked, but it affects both staff and the organisations they work for. In 2024/25 over 900,000 workers experienced work-related stress, anxiety or depression – leading to the loss of 22.1 million working days (HSE, 2025).

I've worked with companies such as LADBible and Genuit Group to provide therapy and support for their employees. Through this work, I've seen fewer mental-health-related absences, smoother returns to work and better staff retention.

Employees have told me they feel less stressed about work and get on better with colleagues. Some say they value the more human approach their organisation has taken.

I work closely with each organisation. Managers can refer someone they think would benefit from therapy, and I can advise HR on supporting staff who are off and planning their return. What's said in sessions stays confidential, and I don't share details with the employer. I also advise organisations more generally on how to support their staff and which practical steps to take first.

Organisations I've worked with have told me that staff in therapy have been more productive and taken less time off. Managers also say they feel more confident supporting people, both at work and while they're off sick.
